text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finns satisfied with first year of EU membership, study shows.
- Large sums of patent money soon to be paid to developers of Raisio's Benecol margarine, says vice president Jukka Maki, admitting compensation should have been paid long ago.
- Finland criticised by nature conservationists for a forestry project in Thailand. They say planning did not sufficiently consider basics of land ownership in Thailand. @
- Finnish government striving to boost its development cooperation funding to 0.4 of GDP by the year 2000.
- Growing number of Finns now firmly believe the economy to pick up next year, an August study reports.
- Justice ministry soon to introduce a new law on sex crime. Spread of child pornographic pictures to be punishable by up to six months imprisonment. @
- Institutional investors have an upbeat view on outlook of the stock market, study shows. Two out of three investors would buy Nokia and 50 percent would sell Amer shares.
- Pressure is mounting for the fourth national TV-channel to be digital. Nokia, for example would benefit from the digitalisation project, spokesman says.

- Trade in Valmet's shares on Wall Street has been modest so far and financial publications in New York have largely ignored the company. Investment bank Smith Barney gives a neutral rating for Valmet in its latest research. @
- Christian League's parliamentary group is planning to seek a confidence vote on unemployment, seeking support from the biggest opposition group the Centre Party.
- Participation in local elections is likely to be more active than in the EU parliament elections, study says. The elections will be held together on October 20.
- Transport of livestock from the Aland islands to mainland Finland has caused an uproar as animals spent over 10 hours crammed up on a ferry.
